title: Investigation of the relevance of increased FVIII activity as a risk factor in venous and arterial thrombosis
summary:
Factor VIII (FVIII) is a coagulation protein which in a state of elevated activity can promote blood clot formation, thus causing deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. Currently, it has not been thoroughly determined whether an elevation in FVIII activity is also associated with arterial occlusion such as heart attack, stroke or peripheral arterial occlusion. 
The study retrospectively analyses data  of patients with a thrombophilia screening in the Hemostaseology Department of the Goethe University clinic Frankfurt between January 2011 and January 2025.  To be included in the study, all patients had to have had at least one arterial or venous vessel occlusion as well as two separate measurements of factor VIII levels ≥ 180%. This study is set to start in 08/2025 and end in 12/2026. 
The goal of this study is to investigate the association between consistently elevated factor VIII levels and the occurrence and recurrence of venous and arterial vascular events. Based on the findings, the study also aims to develop a treatment recommendation.

interventions.name: Patients with thrombosis event, thrombophilia screening and at least two measurement of FVIII acitivity ≥ 180 %

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- thrombosis event
- at least two measurements of FVIII activity ≥180% (IU/dL)
Exclusion criteria:
no thrombosis event, 
FVIII activity < 180 % or FVIII activity ≥ 180 %, but measurement: 
-< 4 weeks past thrombosis event
- during pregnancy or postpartum
- sepsis
- COVID-19 diagnosis
- liver cirrhosis
